# uor-deidentification Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Observation de-identification policy: Publish a collected field only as GDPR Article 4(5) pseudonymised data: suppress content, replace every identifier a platform shows only to its members with a keyed cryptographic hash (the ISO/IEC 20889 pseudonymization technique with a keyed hash, HMAC per FIPS 198-1) whose key is held apart from the corpus, and refuse to publish such an identifier when the key is missing.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Never retain when role is content

The app SHALL NOT answer `retain` when role is content, because content is never published.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `content restricted held` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `retain`
- **AND** the app answers `suppress`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Never retain when role is direct and origin is restricted

The app SHALL NOT answer `retain` when role is direct and origin is restricted, because an identifier a platform shows only to its members is never published as it is.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `direct restricted held` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `retain`
- **AND** the app answers `pseudonymize`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never pseudonymize when key is missing and role is direct and origin is restricted

The app SHALL NOT answer `pseudonymize` when key is missing and role is direct and origin is restricted, because no pseudonym is made without the key.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `direct restricted missing` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `pseudonymize`
- **AND** the app answers `indeterminate`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-001 suppress when role is content

The app SHALL answer `suppress` when role is content, because GDPR Article 5(1)(c) data minimisation and the ISO/IEC 20889 suppression technique: CHAOSS Chat Platform Inclusivity counts messages and participants, never their text or names.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `content restricted held` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `suppress`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 indeterminate when role is direct and origin is restricted and key is missing

The app SHALL answer `indeterminate` when role is direct and origin is restricted and key is missing and no earlier rule matches, because ENISA Pseudonymisation techniques and best practices (2019), Cryptographic hash function: an unkeyed hash of an identifier is reversed by hashing the identifier space, so it is not pseudonymisation under GDPR Article 4(5).

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `direct restricted missing` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `indeterminate`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 pseudonymize when role is direct and origin is restricted

The app SHALL answer `pseudonymize` when role is direct and origin is restricted and no earlier rule matches, because GDPR Article 4(5) and ENISA (2019), Message Authentication Code, and the ISO/IEC 20889 pseudonymization technique: a keyed hash (HMAC-SHA-256, FIPS 198-1) whose key is kept separately and never published.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `direct restricted held` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `pseudonymize`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-004 retain when role is direct and origin is public

The app SHALL answer `retain` when role is direct and origin is public and no earlier rule matches, because LINDDUN Linking and Identifying: the subject published the identifier in the world-readable source the corpus cites, so its digest links nothing the source does not.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule4`).

#### Scenario: REQ-004 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `direct public held` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `retain`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Otherwise retain

The app SHALL answer `retain` when no rule matches, because ISO/IEC 20889 attribute classes: quasi-identifiers the measurement needs and structure that names no person are kept; the keyed pseudonym breaks their linkage to outside data.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `quasi restricted held` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `retain`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `direct restricted missing` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `indeterminate`, decided by REQ-002, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 3 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `pseudonymize`, `suppress`, `retain`, `indeterminate`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `role` | `direct`, `quasi`, `content`, `structural` | the field's ISO/IEC 20889 attribute class: a direct identifier (it names a person or resolves to one, such as a user id, a message id or a thread id), a quasi-identifier (a time or a place a person acted), content the person wrote or named, |
| `origin` | `restricted`, `public` | where the subject published the value: only to the members of a platform (a Discord guild), or in a world-readable source the corpus cites (git commit metadata, a GitHub account) |
| `key` | `held`, `missing` | whether the collection run holds the secret pseudonymisation key |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `pseudonymize` | publish the keyed hash of the value, never the value |
| `suppress` | publish nothing of the value |
| `retain` | publish the value as the source holds it |
| `indeterminate` | no keyed hash can be made, so the record is not published |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 3 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `direct restricted held` gives `pseudonymize`
- `direct restricted missing` gives `indeterminate`
- `direct public held` gives `retain`
- `direct public missing` gives `retain`
- `content restricted held` gives `suppress`
- `content public missing` gives `suppress`
- `quasi restricted held` gives `retain`
- `structural restricted missing` gives `retain`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
